new_statements.quote: Zajkov 1987, 76: «Отпадение конечных гласных в саамском, как и в других финно-угорских языках, можно объяснить, видимо, тем, что ударение, покоящееся на первом слоге, привело сначала к редуцированию конечного гласного, а затем к полному его исчезновению.» [ibid. 73: «Наименее исследованной, по крайней мере, на материале кольско-саамских диалектов, остается акцентно-ритмическая структура слова.»] Kert 1975, 218: «§ 14. Саамский язык имеет связанное ударение (главное) на первом слоге. Это положение верно относительно произнесения отдельных изолированных слов. Второстепенное ударение падает на другие нечетные слоги, кроме последнего.»
new_statements.translation: Zajkov 1987, 76: 'The loss of final vowels in Saami, as in other Finno-Ugric languages, can apparently be explained by the fact that the stress, resting on the first syllable, led first to reduction of the final vowel and then to its complete disappearance.' [ibid. 73: 'The least investigated, at least for the Kola Saami dialects, remains the accentual-rhythmic structure of the word.'] Kert 1975, 218: 'Par. 14. The Saami language has bound (main) stress on the first syllable. This holds for the pronunciation of individual isolated words. Secondary stress falls on the other odd-numbered syllables, except the last.'
new_statements.citation: Zajkov, P. M. 1987. Babinskij dialekt saamskogo jazyka (fonologo-morfologicheskoe issledovanie). Petrozavodsk: Karel'skij filial AN SSSR, Institut jazyka, literatury i istorii. [with the explicit pan-Saami rule in Kert, G. M. 1975. Saamskij jazyk. In: Osnovy finno-ugorskogo jazykoznanija: Pribaltijsko-finskie, saamskij i mordovskie jazyki. Moskva: Nauka, pp. 207, 218]
new_statements.locator: Zajkov 1987 p. 76 (PDF p. 77), ch. I, section 'Struktura absoljutnogo konca slova'; scope disclaimer pp. 72-73 (PDF 73-74). Kert 1975 p. 207 par. 4 and p. 218 par. 14 'Udarenie' (file, PDF pp. 8, 19).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked under (1) Zajkov 1987, : page image pages/ + PDF p.77; printed p.76, confirmed by scanned footers PDF74='73', PDF78='77') shows exactly: 'Отпадение конечных гласных в саамском, как и в других финно-угорских языках, можно объяснить, видимо, тем, что ударение, покоящееся на первом слоге, привело сначала к редуцированию конечного гласного, а затем к полному его исчезновению⁹⁴.' -- verbatim as quoted. Context: section on absolute word-final structure, discussing loss of final vowels specifically in the Babino and Kildin dialects (kehp/keb-i-st etc.); footnote 94 refers to OFUJa 1974 p.203, so the remark is Zajkov's own explanatory sentence leaning on the general Finno-Ugric handbo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress is fixed on the first syllable; per Kert 1975 (stated for all Saami dialects, Akkala/Babino explicitly listed on p. 207) secondary stresses fall on subsequent odd-numbered syllables except a word-final one; stress is non-contrastive ('mechanical'). Zajkov's Akkala monograph presupposes first-syllable stress (p. 76) but deliberately does not describe the accentual-rhythmic structure (pp. 72-73).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Kert 1975 pp. 207, 218 (also Kert 1966: 157, 1971: 122, 1993: 137, all Kildin-based): secondary stress on odd-numbered non-initial syllables except the last (trochaic rhythm). Zajkov 1987 says nothing about secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Kert 1966 p.157 (Kildin-based) excepts loanwords ('за исключением заимствованных слов'); Kert 1975 p.218 notes that stress distribution in words spoken within a phrase differs from isolated words. Zajkov 1987 mentions none.
new_statements.domain_note: Kert 1975: the first-syllable rule holds for isolated (citation-form) words; phrasal stress differs (Aima's five degrees cited for Inari); stresses do not affect meaning; stressed vowels are as a rule longer. Zajkov's remark is diachronic-explanatory (apocope), word domain.
new_statements.identity_note: Zajkov 1987 describes the Babino (бабинский) dialect = Akkala Saami (akka1237), recorded 1971-74 from speakers in Jona (Ёна) resettled from Babino and Girvas (he notes a Girvas sub-variety, гирвозерский говор). His stress remark (p.76) is made for 'Saami' while discussing Babino and Kildin apocope. Kert 1975's explicit rule is scoped over 'all dialects of the Saami language' immediately after a dialect list that names 'В. Диалект Аккала, или бабинские саамы (поселки Ёна и Бабино)'; it is not an Akkala-specific measurement. Halasz 1883 (Glottolog's other akka1237 ref) is in fact Kildin-based and cites Akkala forms only incidentally.

Диалект Аккала, или бабинские саамы'): common to all Saami dialects is main stress on the first syllable and secondary stresses on odd syllables except the last. p.218 par.14 'Ударение': bound main stress on first syllable (isolated words), secondary on other odd syllables except the last; stresses 'mechanical', non-distinctive; stressed vowels usually longer; phrase stress differs (Aima's 5 degrees for Inari). Image-verified.
